title: Lean formalization
headline: Lean 4, 0 sorry, standard axioms: eight claims (Kimura k = mu and fixation probability, Fisher FTNS, Maynard Smith twofold cost, Thompson's cube law, flight power ch02-06, the size limit for flight ch02-07, speed proportional to the square root of size ch02-10) and five extensions (favored fixation floor, blueprint well-formedness, area law, strength law, bending law) (fixation >= i/M when selection does not oppose a mutant; well-formedness of a generated anatomical blueprint). 92 theorems, 53 lemmas; 26 of 26 statement or data mutants rejected, 11/11 controls. NEW: a kernel-checked certificate for the organism thread's flying-fish blueprint: 536 distinct terms, 674 part_of edges, acyclic, every term reaches the body root, 1390 never_in_taxon and 5435 in_taxon statements pinned from Ubergraph exclude nothing, distinct counts per level body 1, organ_system 13, organ 67, tissue 198, cell 257 (the placement-vs-term count the organism thread fixed by hand). Structural only: it does not say the fish is real or the ontology right. Thompson's cube law has a formal statement (exact exponent 3) beside the claims thread's measured exponents (2.74-2.86 on age-bin means; 2.10 to 3.10 by age window). Flying-fish substitution budget still inconclusive. 33 unsigned nanopub drafts pass np check + parse + Delphi lint; no human named; nothing signed or published. Scaling laws R2-R9 from the physics thread are proved in lean/Delphi/Scaling.lean with every contested quantity a named hypothesis: strength and bending complete Galileo's square-cube argument, so 28 constraints rule; on the enumerator's 44 candidates the verdicts are 2 eliminated (both proposed-here), 19 consistent, 23 cannot-rule, and WP-077/C1 (leaf bending) is consistent under the body-like-load reading as the physics thread predicted; nothing in the square-cube rows is eliminated because they restate the laws. Illustrative eliminations: a giant claimed to stand, a glider below its minimum speed, a constant-thickness leaf that still claims a bending limit.
